1. No evidence of intracranial infarction or hemorrhage.
2. 70% stenosis at the origin of the right internal carotid artery by NASCET criteria.
3. The right maxillary sinus is partially opacified with aerosolized secretions raising the possibility of acute sinusitis.
4. New, diffuse tracheal wall thickening with a small amount of aerosolized secretions in the upper thoracic trachea raises the possibility of tracheitis.
5. Limited evaluation of the lung apices in the setting of respiratory motion artifact.
However, multiple millimetric pulmonary nodules are seen and better assessed on concurrent chest CT.
6. 3 mm of anterolisthesis of C2 on C3 is likely chronic given associated degenerative changes and a lack of prevertebral soft tissue swelling.
However, recommend correlation with symptoms in the absence of prior imaging for comparison.
7. Moderate to severe multilevel cervical spondylosis includes at least mild spinal canal narrowing at C2-C3 and severe neural foraminal narrowing on the left at C3-C4.
If clinically indicated, consider cervical spine MRI for further evaluation.
8. T4 vertebral body age indeterminate anterior compression deformity, with no definite evidence of bony retropulsion.
If clinically indicated, thoracic spine MRI may be obtained for further evaluation.
